get.description:
Price history, clamped to the caller's plan window.

Deliberately still @Public: an anonymous visitor gets the free-tier window
of *real* data rather than a login wall, which is what makes the product
indexable and worth sharing. The response states the window it actually
covered and whether it was truncated, so the UI can offer the upgrade
honestly instead of silently showing a short chart.

post.description:
Not gated on a feature flag: the seat *count* is the limit, and
OrganizationsService.addMember already refuses when they are used up.
Requiring FEATURES.TEAM_SEATS here locked the Seller plan out of the
three seats it pays for, because that flag only exists on Enterprise.

get.description:
The only way out to a retailer's site. Always records a click and
always redirects through the generated affiliate URL -- never the raw
SourceListing.externalUrl directly. Public: anonymous visitors can
click "Go to Store" too, so auth here is best-effort (see
extractOptionalUserId), not required.

post.description:
Inbound postback target: register this URL (with ?secret=... baked in)
as the network's Action Tracker / postback callback. Public route, but
the shared secret stands in for real request auth since the network
calls this anonymously.

get.description:
Everything the client needs to decide what to show: the resolved plan,
the limits, and live usage counts so the UI can render "7 of 10 tracked"
without a second round trip.

post.description: Stripe-hosted billing portal: card updates, invoices, self-cancel.

get.description: Polled by the navbar bell; deliberately tiny.

The full intelligence panel for a product.

Authenticated but not feature-gated: the history window is already
clamped per plan inside the service, so a free user gets a real (shorter)
answer rather than a locked panel. That is the funnel — showing a genuine
30-day verdict is what makes the 365-day one worth paying for.
The Buy/Wait call on its own, for compact placements like cards.

The Deal Hunter itself.

A paid feature: it is the single most expensive read in the consumer
product (a history series per candidate), and it is the clearest
expression of what the subscription is for.

Throttled more tightly than the default because each call fans out to
dozens of per-product history queries.

Shows what the parser understood, without running a search.

Public and cheap: it powers live "we read this as ..." feedback as the
user types, which is what makes a natural-language box trustworthy rather
than a black box. It reveals nothing about pricing.

info.title: PriceLens API
info.description: Cross-platform price comparison API: one canonical product per item, with every store listing matched to it and its price history.

tags.name: affiliate
tags.description: Affiliate link tracking, store redirects and conversions

tags.name: api-keys
tags.description: Workspace API keys for the partner API

password.description: Min 8 chars, must contain letter and number

canonicalProductId.description: The product to attach the listing to. Required to accept an item that proposed none.

platformSlugs.description: Store slugs to sweep; all enabled stores when omitted.

dryRun.description: Only log proposed merges. Defaults to RECONCILIATION_DRY_RUN.

thresholdValue.description:
A target price, an absolute drop, or a percentage, depending on
`alertType`. Ignored for RESTOCK, which fires on a stock transition.

repeatable.description: Re-arm after firing instead of parking in TRIGGERED.

cooldownHours.description: Minimum hours between notifications for a repeating alert.

platformId.description: The tracked store that is this seller's own, when we crawl it.

targetMarginPct.description: Percentages of price, not of cost.

providerKey.description: Which AffiliateProvider builds the links, e.g. "amazon".

trackingParams.description: Extra query parameters added to every outbound link.

immediately.description: Default is cancel-at-period-end; the user keeps what they paid for.

days.description: Overrides the plan's interval for hand-sold contracts.

code.description: Empty for Telegram, where the code is sent to the bot rather than typed here.
